description: List messages in the user's inbox (default mail folder)
notes: Defaults to top 25 messages ordered by most recent. Use $top to control page size (max 1000). The bodyPreview field returns first 255 characters.

description: List messages in a specific mail folder by folder ID
examples: Show me messages in folder AAMkAG...
List emails in this folder ID
Get messages from a specific folder
notes: Replace {folder_id} with the actual folder ID. Use /me/mailFolders to discover folder IDs first.

description: List messages in the Sent Items folder
examples: What emails have I sent recently?
notes: Well-known folder name 'sentitems' can be used directly in the URL instead of a folder ID.

description: List messages in the Drafts folder
notes: Well-known folder name 'drafts' can be used directly. Draft messages have isDraft=true.

description: List messages in the Deleted Items (trash) folder
notes: Well-known folder name 'deleteditems' maps to Deleted Items / Trash.

description: List messages in the Junk Email (spam) folder
notes: Well-known folder name 'junkemail' maps to Junk Email / Spam.

description: List messages in the Archive folder
notes: Well-known folder name 'archive' maps to the Archive folder. Not all mailboxes have an archive folder enabled.

description: Get a single email message by ID with full body content
examples: Show me the full email with ID AAMkAG...
Get the details of this email
Show me the body of this email
notes: Returns the full message including body content. The body.content field contains HTML by default. Add Prefer: outlook.body-content-type="text" header to get plain text instead.

description: Search messages across all folders using KQL (Keyword Query Language) via $search
examples: Search my emails for project update
Search for emails mentioning quarterly report
Look through my mail for contract
notes: The $search parameter uses KQL syntax. Pass the query in double quotes. $search and $filter CANNOT be combined on /me/messages. $search automatically searches across subject, body, and sender. Results are ranked by relevance, not date.

description: Search messages from a specific sender using $search with from: KQL keyword
examples: Show me emails sent by my manager
notes: Use from: KQL keyword inside $search to filter by sender. Example: $search="from:john@contoso.com". You can also use display names: $search="from:John Smith". Cannot combine $search with $filter.

description: Search messages by subject line using $search with subject: KQL keyword
examples: Find emails with subject containing meeting notes
Search for emails with 'invoice' in the subject
Look for messages about weekly standup in subject
notes: Use subject: KQL keyword inside $search to search only the subject field. Cannot combine $search with $filter.

description: Search for messages that have attachments using $search with hasAttachments: KQL keyword
examples: Search for messages that have files attached
Show me emails with attachments about the project
notes: Use hasAttachments:true inside $search. Can be combined with other KQL keywords like from: or subject: within the same $search string. Cannot combine $search with $filter.

description: Filter messages to show only unread emails
examples: How many unread messages do I have?
notes: Use $filter with isRead eq false. $filter can be combined with $orderby but NOT with $search. You can also add $count=true to get the total count of unread messages.

description: Filter messages by importance level (high, normal, low)
notes: Valid importance values: 'low', 'normal', 'high'. The value must be quoted in the filter expression. Can combine with other $filter clauses using 'and'.

description: Filter messages received within a specific date range
examples: Show me emails from last week
Get emails between March 1 and March 15
notes: Use receivedDateTime with ge (greater than or equal) and lt (less than) operators. Dates must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone (Z for UTC). Can combine with other filters using 'and'.

description: Send a new email message
examples: Compose and send a new email
Send a message to my team
notes: sendMail returns 202 Accepted with no response body. Set saveToSentItems to false to skip saving in Sent Items. contentType can be 'HTML' or 'Text'.

description: Send a new email with CC and BCC recipients
examples: Send an email with CC to my manager
Email john with CC to sarah and BCC to admin
Send a message and copy my team
Compose an email with CC and blind copy
notes: sendMail returns 202 Accepted with no response body. CC recipients are visible to all; BCC recipients are hidden. All recipient arrays follow the same format.

description: Reply to a specific email message
examples: Send a reply to this message
notes: The comment field is the reply body text (plain text). The toRecipients in the message object is optional and overrides the default reply-to address. Returns 202 Accepted with no body.

description: Reply all to an email message, responding to all recipients
examples: Respond to everyone on this thread
notes: Replies to the sender and all toRecipients and ccRecipients. The comment field is the reply body (plain text). Returns 202 Accepted with no body.

description: Forward an email message to other recipients
examples: Send this message to someone else
Pass this email along to the team
notes: The comment field is optional text prepended to the forwarded message. toRecipients is required. Returns 202 Accepted with no body.

description: Create a new draft email message in the Drafts folder
examples: Start composing an email but don't send it
notes: Creating a message via POST to /me/messages saves it as a draft (isDraft=true). To send it later, use POST /me/messages/{id}/send. importance can be 'low', 'normal', or 'high'.

description: Update an existing draft email message
examples: Change the subject of my draft
notes: Only draft messages (isDraft=true) can have their content updated. You can update subject, body, recipients, importance, and other writable properties. Include only the fields you want to change.

description: Delete an email message (moves to Deleted Items)
notes: Moves the message to the Deleted Items folder. Returns 204 No Content. To permanently delete, delete from the Deleted Items folder.

description: Move a message to a different mail folder
examples: Move this email to the archive
Move this message to a folder
File this email in my Projects folder
notes: destinationId can be a folder ID or a well-known folder name (inbox, sentitems, drafts, deleteditems, junkemail, archive). Returns the moved message object with updated parentFolderId.

description: Copy a message to another mail folder
examples: Copy this email to my archive
Duplicate this message to another folder
Make a copy of this email in my Projects folder
notes: destinationId can be a folder ID or a well-known folder name. Returns a copy of the message in the destination folder with a new ID.

description: Flag an email message for follow-up
examples: Add a flag to this email
notes: flagStatus values: 'notFlagged', 'flagged', 'complete'. You can optionally include startDateTime and dueDateTime in the flag object for timed follow-ups.

description: Remove the flag from an email message
examples: Remove the flag from this message
Mark this flag as not flagged
notes: Set flagStatus to 'notFlagged' to remove the flag. Use 'complete' to mark the flag as completed instead of removing it.

description: Mark an email message as read
notes: Sets isRead to true. Returns the updated message object.

description: Mark an email message as unread
notes: Sets isRead to false. Returns the updated message object.

description: List top-level mail folders in the mailbox
notes: Returns top-level folders only. Use /me/mailFolders/{id}/childFolders to get subfolders. Well-known folder names: inbox, sentitems, drafts, deleteditems, junkemail, archive.

description: List child (sub) folders of a specific mail folder
examples: Show me subfolders of my inbox
List child folders of this folder
What subfolders are in this mail folder?
notes: Replace {folder_id} with a folder ID or a well-known folder name. To get subfolders of Inbox, use /me/mailFolders/inbox/childFolders.

description: Create a new top-level mail folder
examples: Create a new email folder called Projects
Add a folder to my mailbox
Create an email folder named Clients
notes: Creates a top-level folder under the mailbox root. Set isHidden to true to create a hidden folder. Returns the created folder object with its ID.

description: Create a child (sub) folder under an existing mail folder
examples: Create a subfolder under my Projects folder
Make a new folder inside inbox
Add a child folder to this mail folder
notes: Creates a subfolder inside the specified parent folder. The parent can be identified by folder ID or well-known name (e.g., inbox).

description: Delete a mail folder and all its contents
examples: Delete a folder from my mailbox
notes: Permanently deletes the folder and all its contents (messages and child folders). Returns 204 No Content. Cannot delete well-known folders (inbox, sentitems, etc.).

description: Rename a mail folder
examples: Rename my Projects folder to Active Projects
Change the name of this mail folder
notes: Updates the displayName of the folder. Cannot rename well-known folders (inbox, sentitems, etc.). Returns the updated folder object.

description: List all Outlook categories defined for the user
notes: Returns all categories defined in the user's master category list. Each category has a displayName and color. Colors are preset values like 'preset0' through 'preset24'.

description: Create a new Outlook category
examples: Create a new email category called Important Clients
Add a new category with a red color
notes: Color values are preset strings: 'preset0' (red) through 'preset24'. Use 'none' for no color. Category displayName must be unique.

description: Delete an Outlook category
examples: Get rid of this email category
notes: The category_id is the URL-encoded displayName of the category. Returns 204 No Content. Deleting a category does not remove it from messages that already have it assigned.

description: Assign categories to an email message
examples: Add the 'Urgent' category to this email
Tag this message with a category
notes: The categories property is an array of category displayName strings. This REPLACES all existing categories. To add a category, first GET the message to read existing categories, then include them all in the PATCH. Categories must exist in the master category list.

description: Remove all categories from an email message
examples: Clear the labels on this message
Remove all tags from this message
notes: Set categories to an empty array to remove all. To remove only specific categories, GET the message first, then PATCH with the remaining categories you want to keep.

description: List all attachments on an email message
examples: Show me the attachments on this email
What files are attached to this message?
notes: Returns file attachments, item attachments (embedded messages), and reference attachments (links to cloud files). The contentBytes field contains base64-encoded file content but is not returned by default in list operations.

description: Get a specific attachment from an email message including its content
examples: Get the file attached to this email
notes: Returns the full attachment including contentBytes (base64-encoded). For large attachments (>3MB), use the /$value endpoint to stream the raw bytes. The @odata.type indicates the attachment type: #microsoft.graph.fileAttachment, #microsoft.graph.itemAttachment, or #microsoft.graph.referenceAttachment.

description: Add a file attachment to a draft email message
examples: Attach a file to my draft
Add an attachment to this draft email
Upload a file to this draft message
notes: contentBytes must be base64-encoded. The message must be a draft (isDraft=true). For files larger than 3MB, use the upload session API instead. contentType is the MIME type (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/png').

description: List all inbox rules (mail flow rules)
examples: What mail rules do I have?
notes: Returns all rules that apply to the inbox. Each rule has conditions, actions, and exceptions. Rules are evaluated in order of their sequence property.

description: Get a specific inbox rule by ID
examples: Show me the details of this inbox rule
What does this mail rule do?
notes: Returns the full rule definition including conditions, actions, and exceptions.

description: Create a new inbox rule to automatically process incoming messages
examples: Create a rule to move emails from john@contoso.com to my Projects folder
Set up an inbox rule to mark newsletters as read
Make a rule to flag emails with 'urgent' in the subject
notes: Include only the conditions and actions you need. The sequence determines rule evaluation order (lower numbers run first). moveToFolder requires a folder ID, not a well-known name. Set stopProcessingRules to true to prevent subsequent rules from running.

description: Delete an inbox rule
examples: Get rid of this mail rule
notes: Permanently deletes the rule. Returns 204 No Content.

description: Send a previously created draft email message
examples: Send the draft message I created
notes: The message must be a draft (isDraft=true). Returns 202 Accepted with no response body. The message is moved to Sent Items after sending.

description: Create a draft reply to a message (without sending)
examples: Create a draft reply to this email
Start a reply but don't send it yet
Draft a response to this message
notes: Creates a draft reply in the Drafts folder. The toRecipients override is optional. Use /me/messages/{draft_id}/send to send later. The comment field sets the initial reply body.

description: Create a draft reply-all to a message (without sending)
examples: Draft a reply to all recipients
Start a reply all but don't send yet
notes: Creates a draft reply-all in the Drafts folder. Includes all original toRecipients and ccRecipients. Use /me/messages/{draft_id}/send to send later.

description: Create a draft forward of a message (without sending)
examples: Create a draft forward of this email
Prepare to forward this email but don't send yet
notes: Creates a draft forward in the Drafts folder. The toRecipients and comment can be set here or added later by updating the draft. Use /me/messages/{draft_id}/send to send later.

description: List messages across all folders (not scoped to inbox)
examples: Show me all my messages across all folders
List all emails regardless of folder
Search through all my mail folders
notes: Unlike /me/mailFolders/inbox/messages, this endpoint searches across ALL folders. Useful when you don't know which folder a message is in. The parentFolderId tells you which folder each message belongs to.

description: Get a specific mail folder by ID or well-known name
examples: Get the details of this mail folder
Show me the inbox folder info
How many messages are in this folder?
notes: Can use a folder ID or well-known folder name (inbox, sentitems, drafts, deleteditems, junkemail, archive). Returns totalItemCount and unreadItemCount for quick counts.

description: Update a mail folder's properties
examples: Change the display name of this folder
Modify the properties of a mail folder
notes: Currently only displayName can be updated. Cannot modify well-known folders.

description: Mark a flagged email as complete
examples: Mark this flagged email as complete
Complete the follow-up on this email
I'm done with this flagged message
notes: Sets the flagStatus to 'complete', which shows a checkmark instead of a flag. The three states are: 'notFlagged', 'flagged', 'complete'.

description: Filter messages that are flagged for follow-up
notes: Use flag/flagStatus eq 'flagged' to find flagged items. Use 'complete' to find completed flags. Can be combined with other $filter clauses using 'and'.

description: Filter messages that have attachments using $filter
examples: List messages that have files attached
Find emails with attachments in my inbox
notes: Uses $filter (not $search) to find messages with attachments in a specific folder. Unlike the $search approach, this can be combined with other $filter clauses and $orderby.

description: Get internet message headers for an email (for troubleshooting delivery issues)
examples: Get the internet headers for this message
notes: internetMessageHeaders contains an array of {name, value} objects with SMTP headers. Useful for troubleshooting delivery, verifying SPF/DKIM, or finding the original sender behind forwarded messages.

description: Get the raw MIME content of an email message
examples: Get the raw MIME content of this email
Download the .eml file for this message
notes: Returns the raw MIME content (RFC 2822 format) of the message. The response Content-Type is application/octet-stream. Useful for exporting emails or processing with other mail tools.
